title: The design system requires the Inter font to be loaded by the host application, with preconnect link tags recommended over a CSS import
content:
`@powerhousedao/design-system` contains "base and scoped (project) components, utilities, and hooks for the powerhouse org" — and its one hard setup requirement is a font.

The design system uses the **Inter** font family and does not ship it. A consumer picks one of two approaches:

**Option 1 (recommended) — HTML link tags** in `<head>`, with preconnects for performance:

```html
<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com" />
<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.gstatic.com" crossorigin />
<link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Inter:ital,opsz,wght@0,14..32,100..900;1,14..32,100..900&display=swap" rel="stylesheet" />
```

**Option 2 — a CSS `@import`**, described as the fallback.

The distinction matters more than it looks: a CSS import blocks on the stylesheet before the font request begins, which is exactly the render delay the preconnect pair avoids. And the variable-font axes in that URL (`opsz`, `wght` ranges) are what the design system's typography scale expects — substituting a static Inter weight silently changes the rendering.

The "base and scoped" split is the other thing to know: the package carries both the neutral primitives and project-scoped components, which is why an editor importing from it can pick up Connect-specific styling.
